lead: Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar' or 'Trenevar') is a steroid that is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. Users who take prohormones of this type aim for a leaner, more muscular physique, and one T Nation member described a 'shredded' look after using it.[1][5]

The proposed chain is that the body converts a precursor into the active steroid, in the way androstenedione relates to testosterone; Wikipedia draws this comparison.[1] In receptor assays trendione itself binds androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold less strongly than trenbolone.[1][3]

Most published work on it concerns environmental fate: trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant, and trendione is excreted in manure and studied in soil and runoff.[2][4] It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1] No human trials of trendione have been published.

Trenbolone itself, the parent compound, was first synthesised in 1963, has veterinary use as a cattle growth implant and was never approved for human use; it is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US [7]. Trendione's role in that story is as one of its metabolites, which is why researchers studying cattle manure and runoff measure it alongside 17-alpha and 17-beta trenbolone [2][4].

angle.text: Supplement users take it hoping to build muscle and lose fat, as a precursor to the potent anabolic steroid trenbolone. Reports of its effects come from user anecdotes rather than studies.

infobox: Listed in the 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act[1]

paras: Wikipedia classes trendione as an androgen, anabolic steroid and progestogen prohormone and describes it as inactive itself, with affinity for the androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold lower than trenbolone.[1] A receptor study found the affinity of the major trenbolone metabolites, including trendione, was under 5 percent of that of 17beta-trenbolone.[3]

In humans given labelled 17-beta-trenbolone as a tracer, 54 percent of the radioactivity appeared in urine within 26 hours and 63 percent within 72 hours; more than half of the urinary material was glucuronide conjugates containing mainly 17-alpha-trenbolone, 17-beta-trenbolone and trendione [8]. The authors noted that disposition in humans differs significantly from that in rats [8]. Wikipedia's trenbolone article says that studies disagree about whether trenbolone is converted by aromatase or 5-alpha-reductase, and that the popular claim that it is five times as potent as testosterone is not established, with rat studies suggesting roughly three to five times [7].

Wikipedia describes trendione as being to trenbolone what androstenedione is to testosterone: a prohormone that is itself largely inactive and would need to be converted in the body to act [1]. How efficiently, or whether, this conversion happens after oral intake by people has not been reported.

Wikipedia describes it as a designer steroid sold online as a dietary supplement.[1] On T Nation, a poster listing past anabolic use said low-dose 'trenevar' in 2015 helped them get very lean.[5] Another thread asks how long trendione and related products remain traceable in the body.[6]
The same Wikipedia article cites a 2016 Military Medicine case report of acute pancreatitis linked to a supplement containing anabolic-androgenic steroids.[1]

Trenbolone's own history includes veterinary use in cattle and a human clinical ester that is no longer marketed, according to Wikipedia; sport authorities list doping cases involving the parent drug [7]. Trendione-type products are sold as prohormone supplements marketed under names such as Trenavar, and the product is named in the US 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act [1].
Trendione is named in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1]

Trenbolone acetate has been used as a growth promoter in US beef cattle since 1987 [9]. Studies of implanted cattle identify 17-alpha-trenbolone and trendione as the main metabolites in manure. In a mass-balance study of manure from cattle implanted with 40 mg of trenbolone acetate and 8 mg of estradiol, a maximum of 9.3 percent of the implant dose was excreted as 17-alpha-trenbolone over 113 days, and under 1 percent as 17-beta-trenbolone or trendione [11]. Research has examined how they degrade in agricultural soils, sorb to soil and break down under light [2][4].

In aerobic water microcosms dosed with about 1,400 ng/L of the metabolites, observed half-lives at 20 C were about 0.9 days for 17-beta-trenbolone, 1.3 days for trendione and 2.2 days for 17-alpha-trenbolone, with longer half-lives in colder conditions [12]. In a 14-day study, adult female medaka fish exposed to the metabolites showed changes in ovarian follicles, and trendione reduced whole-body estradiol and testosterone [9]. A study of a Midwest tile-drained farm receiving animal waste measured hormone discharge to the receiving drainage [10].

No studies found of trendione in people as a supplement or drug. The published literature consists of receptor-binding assays [3], one human tracer study of its parent compound that detected trendione as a urinary metabolite [8], and environmental and animal studies [2][4][9][11][12].

Trenbolone acetate in use as a beef-cattle growth promoter in the US [9].
Trendione named in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act.[1]

claims.claim: Trendione ('Trenavar') produces a lean, shredded physique
claims.believers: A T Nation poster wrote that low-dose trenevar in 2015 'really made me lean'.[5]
claims.experts: No published human study has tested trendione; receptor assays show it binds hormone receptors far more weakly than trenbolone.[1][3]

claims.claim: Prohormones like this convert to trenbolone in the body.
claims.believers: Users reason by analogy with androstenedione and testosterone and report lean physiques on products they call Trenavar [5].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes trendione as largely inactive itself with more than 100-fold lower receptor affinity than trenbolone [1]; no published human study has measured conversion after oral intake of trendione.

name: Trendione

card.summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold as a prohormone; studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.
card.note: Listed in the US 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act.

quick.overview:
Trendione is a trenbolone metabolite that has been sold online as a prohormone supplement. It is listed in the US 2014 designer steroid law.

No human studies exist.
quick.mechanism: It is inactive by itself in receptor assays; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone.
quick.risks: No human safety data. Legal restrictions apply in the US.
